note: Fast runs both ways: the nine-note run up and back, a falling minor pentatonic run landing on the 3rd with the metronome, then the book's pentatonic run that climbs and falls with the metronome under it. The old Stage selector of tempos is now moves (any key, 60 to 90 bpm), every tool written at 60; each run step states its range and the semitone climb, and the pentatonic run is described as the book writes it.

exercise.title: Fast runs, rising and falling
exercise.why: A falling run tends to go flat as it drops, so the way down gets a drill of its own on the metronome, landing on one note you can check.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the run: two chords set the key, and the mic starts with them. The run goes from Do up to Re above the high Do and back, four notes per beat both ways, and each pass starts a semitone higher, the last one reaching the top of your range. Sing it on "ah", and close towards "oo" at the top.
Practice until the way down is as even as the way up.

Press Start exercise below: the metronome and the mic start together, at {{=bpm}}. From the high {{1}}, sing {{1}}, {{b7}}, {{5}}, {{4}} in one beat and land on the ringed {{b3}} on the next, then step down to the low {{1}} and hold it. Sing it on "oo".
Practice until {{b3}} lands on the click and in tune.
{{?bpm}}At a faster tempo the low notes of the run sag first, so listen to those.

Press Play below to hear the run with the metronome under it: the mic starts with it. The run climbs from Mi to the high Do, falls back through Sol and Mi, dips to La under Do and lands on Do, and each pass starts a semitone higher, the last one reaching the top of your range. Sing it on "ah".
If a pass falls behind the beat, sing only its first note on each beat, then put the rest back in.
